summary: Intermittent streaming pause when client performs large multipart upload (upload backpressure affects SSE/WebSocket generation)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that chat streaming (SSE and websocket) stalls mid-generation when the client simultaneously uploads a large file (50–200MB) in the same HTTP session. Impact: Users see streaming silence for 5–30+ seconds followed by either resume or connection close depending on client timeout. Environment: prod us-west on Redwood hosted API. Intermittent; appears correlated with client-initiated multipart/form-data uploads that run concurrently with open server-sent streaming responses.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming chat request via SSE to redwood-instruct-v1 with long expected output (>600 tokens).

2) While the stream is active (after first few tokens), the client initiates a multipart/form-data POST of a 100MB file to an unrelated endpoint in the same TCP connection (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive) or via same browser tab that reuses connection resources.

3) Observe streaming silence after ~4–12 seconds of concurrent upload. Client eventually times out or receives a socket close. Repro rate ~7/20 attempts in customer's environment. Not reproducible consistently in our internal lab without mimicking slow upload throughput and limited socket buffers.
4) Variations: reproduces with both SSE and websocket streaming; less likely when upload is fast or when upload is performed on a separate connection (new TCP/TLS).

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Client-side upload is saturating socket send/receive buffers on the shared connection, causing kernel-level backpressure and preventing timely flush of streamed SSE/WebSocket frames from serving-runtime.
Reproduced locally by throttling upload to 10–30KB/s while multiplexing SSE and upload on same connection: observed identical mid-generation stalls and EAGAIN on write syscalls in runtime logs.
The api-gateway currently reuses connections for keep-alive; HTTP/1.1 clients that do large uploads can block other writes if they run on same connection and OS-level buffers are small.
Serving-runtime observed increased write retry counts but correctly queued tokens; no model hang inside runtime. Worker remained CPU-bound but had tokens queued for emit.
No evidence of model-level timeouts or kernel OOM. Memory and GPU metrics normal. Network socket buffer utilization high during incidents.

Customer browser stack: uses an SDK that reuses the same XHR/fetch connection for uploads in a way that results in a single TCP connection being congested. Mobile app shows similar behavior when using HTTP/1.1. HTTP/2 mitigates but customer is on HTTP/1.1 via older proxy.
mitigation: Short-term workaround recommended to customer: perform uploads on a separate connection (open a new TCP/TLS session) or upgrade to HTTP/2 where stream multiplexing is handled differently. Also advise client-side upload throttling or splitting uploads into smaller chunks and using a separate domain/endpoint to avoid keep-alive reuse. We toggled a gateway flag to limit connection reuse for the customer's IP temporarily (rate-limited); that reduced reproductions from 35% -> 6% during the observation window.
resolution: Engineering action items committed: (1) Add server-side heuristic to deprioritize large client-initiated uploads on connections with active streaming responses — if a large upload is detected, prefer to route it to a new connection or refuse keep-alive reuse for parallel streams. (2) Add backpressure metrics to streaming dashboards (socket write EAGAIN counts, retry counts) and alert when thresholds exceeded. (3) Documentation: update streaming best-practices to advise separate connections for concurrent uploads. Patch PR merged to api-gateway: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-gateway/pull/2789; will roll to canary on 2026-03-16 and full prod rollout 2026-03-18.
